'''Ownellco'''<ref name="Mythe" /> was a [[Lutrillian]] that spent time in [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]] in [[Mos Eisley]] [[spaceport]] on the [[planet]] [[Tatooine]]<ref name="ANH" /> in [[1 BBY]].<ref name="Atlas">{{FilmDate|IV|1|Ownellco's appearance}}</ref> When the local [[moisture farmer]] [[Luke Skywalker]] and his [[droid]]s [[R2-D2]] and [[C-3PO]] entered the [[cantina]], Ownellco was stood with<ref name="ANH" /> the [[Qiraash]] [[Leesub Sirln]]<ref name="SWCT">{{SWCT|set=Base Series 3|cardname=Leesub Sirln}}</ref> near one of the establishment's tables. Ownellco then moved across the room and sat with a drink in [[Limb|hand]] at a table between two of the cantina's booths with another Lutrillian, looking up at Skywalker as the moisture farmer approached the bar.<ref name="ANH" />

The Lutrillian later left the cantina<ref name="ANH" /> and walked past Skywalker and the [[Jedi]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]]<ref name="Mythe" /> as they hurried through the streets of Mos Eisley toward [[Docking Bay 94]].<ref name="ANH" /> Ownellco had fair skin, [[Color|brown]] [[hair]] and black [[eye]]s.<ref name="Mythe" /> While in Mos Eisley the Lutrillian wore a light brown [[jacket]], black pants, and a cream [[Scarf|ascot]].<ref name="ANH" />

==Behind the scenes==
Ownellco was created for the [[1977]] [[original trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']].<ref name="ANH" /> Two Lutrillian costumes were created for the film by creature designer [[Stuart Freeborn]] based on a costume sketch by concept artist [[John Mollo]].<ref name="Chronicle">''[[Star Wars Chronicles]]''</ref> Mollo's name for Ownellco was "Colonel", which was used on set.<ref name="Mythe" />

In the new ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], the character was first identified as Ownellco in the [[2016]] reference book ''[[Star Wars, Objets du mythe]]'', which was written by [[Patrice Girod]] and [[Arnaud Grunberg]]. The name was based on the original "Colonel" name,<ref name="Mythe" /> and originated in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, where it was first used in the article "[[Rogues Gallery (department)|Rogues Gallery: The Unusual Suspects: Who's Who in Mos Eisley]]," which was written by [[Leland Chee]] and published in [[Star Wars Insider 130|''Star Wars Insider'' 130]] on [[December 13]], [[2011]].<ref name="Insider">{{InsiderCite|130|Rogues Gallery|Rogues Gallery: The Unusual Suspects: Who's Who in Mos Eisley}}</ref>
